scope: Local source, authorization and browser-boundary tests, complete deterministic and Chromium suites, a fresh isolated checksum-enabled PostgreSQL exercise, strict policy validators, and production-build evidence for immutable revision of a pending resolution proposal. Synthetic tenants, identities, financial values, proposals, approvals, and audit events only. No customer data, provider system, protected staging, compliance, reliability, or production-readiness claim is included.

requirement.priorGap: The workflow protected proposal evidence from mutation but allowed a new version only after rejection or automatic supersession; an original proposer could not correct a pending proposal.

decisions.existingDatabaseAuthority: Migration 0015 already permits the superseded lifecycle status, protects proposal evidence from update/delete, and makes approvals append-only and proposal-version-bound.

atomicTransition: lock the tenant-scoped exception authority row
change only the old proposal lifecycle status to superseded
compute max historical version plus one
insert a new proposal UUID/version with immutable evidence
recompute required approvals from the current organization review policy
retain the exception in proposed state
append one reasoned resolution.revised audit event before commit

concurrency.allowedConcurrentApprovalOutcome: The approval either commits against the old version before supersession or is rejected after supersession.
concurrency.forbiddenOutcome: No approval can attach to or count toward the replacement version.

bootstrapDriftFoundAndFixed.initialObservedFailure: Migration 0051 correctly refused to apply because the API repository integration bootstrap had not created the required reconai_maintenance role.
bootstrapDriftFoundAndFixed.fix: The bootstrap now creates the bounded no-bypass-RLS maintenance login and grants only database connect and schema usage before migrations.

finalGate.command: DATABASE_ADMIN_URL=[isolated local administrator URL] DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL=[isolated local migrator URL] DATABASE_URL=[isolated local application URL] pnpm exec vitest run --project integration apps/api/src/repository.integration.test.ts
revisionAssertions: old approval remains version-bound historical evidence
revision audit previous and new values match the transition
two distinct reviewers approve only the replacement version
simultaneous approval and revision preserve one pending replacement with zero transferred approvals
tenant-scoped exception detail derives canRevise per actor

focusedGate.command: pnpm exec vitest run apps/api/src/app.tenant.test.ts apps/web/src/tenant-read-response.test.ts apps/web/src/app/api/recon/actions/route.test.ts

knownLimitations: This local proof does not establish representative multi-replica contention, managed PostgreSQL behavior, protected-ingress behavior, or staging review-race timing.

A revision reevaluates the current organization approval policy. Policy history and the exact required count remain recorded on each immutable proposal, but a policy change may intentionally make the replacement stricter or less strict than its predecessor.
The browser can revise only proposal types it explicitly supports; an unknown existing type remains visible and is preserved unless the operator deliberately selects a supported replacement type.
The strict browser read schema must be updated deliberately when proposal state or operator-visible fields change; unknown upstream fields remain discarded.
This increment does not close provider sandbox, protected-staging, owner-policy, support-operations, authentication-stack, or release-integrity findings.
One local workstation run is not CI, staging, reliability, capacity, compliance, legal-fulfillment, or production-readiness evidence.
conclusion: The Milestone 1 proposal-edit requirement is now implemented locally as original-proposer-only immutable replacement. Old evidence and approvals remain historical and version-bound, the replacement starts with zero approval authority, approval/revision lock ordering is serialized, the BFF does not expose proposer identity, and API, Chromium, and fresh PostgreSQL race tests pass. Goal 1 remains active; provider, owner, distributed-runtime, maintained-authentication-stack, and protected-staging gates remain open.
